flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: What is a guardrail, and what are the four verbs every guardrail performs?
flashcards.a: Deterministic input/output validation and policy enforcement wrapped around a nondeterministic model. Four verbs: CLASSIFY (topic, PII, jailbreak, toxicity), VERIFY (schema, facts, constraints), TRANSFORM (redact, mask, pseudonymize), ROUTE (pass, block, fix, escalate to human). The libraries are prebuilt validators; the engineering is choosing WHERE they run, what they cost, and their failure policy.

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: Name the three validator families with latency and coverage characteristics.
flashcards.a: Deterministic (regex, schema, checksums, blocklists, canaries): sub-millisecond, in-process, high precision on well-formed identifiers, no semantics. Statistical (Presidio-style pattern + context words + optional NER): ~50-300 ms, tunable per-entity confidence thresholds. Model-based (Llama Guard, omni-moderation): hundreds of ms, a full model forward pass, covers semantics (novel jailbreaks, paraphrased toxicity). Rule: never pay tier-3 cost for a tier-1 guarantee; always prefilter before the classifier.

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: Give the Llama Guard 3 headline numbers and what they compare against.
flashcards.a: 8B Llama-3.1 fine-tune, 14 hazard categories (S1-S14, MLCommons taxonomy + Code Interpreter Abuse), 8 languages. On Meta's English response-classification benchmark: F1 0.939 / FPR 0.040, vs Llama Guard 2 at 0.877 / 0.081 and GPT-4 zero-shot at 0.805 / 0.152. INT8 variant is ~40% smaller for cheaper deployment. Meta trained it on benign borderline data specifically to suppress false positives.

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: How does Llama Guard mechanically classify prompts vs responses, and how do you get a score?
flashcards.a: The same model emits 'safe' or 'unsafe' plus violated categories; prompt classification and response classification use DIFFERENT policies applied via the chat template. Input filtering catches harm before the model responds; output filtering lets the model attempt a safe answer and censors only the result; Meta recommends both. Score = probability of the FIRST generated token, thresholded by you. Note: it is itself an LLM and jailbreakable, so it is a layer, not a boundary.

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: How does Presidio detect PII, and why is the German postcode recognizer a good example?
flashcards.a: Analyzer runs a recognizer ensemble: pattern match plus checksums plus context words plus optional NER, each span scored with a confidence. Anonymizer applies operators to detected spans. DE_PLZ is the instructive case: 5 digits alone is a terrible signal, so its base confidence is 0.05 and it only produces actionable results when address-context words are present. Context suppression is how you tune per-entity false positives.

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: What pseudonymization discipline is required to avoid the de-anonymization trap?
flashcards.a: Per-request map keyed by TOKEN (never span index), never logged, destroyed after render. Re-hydration happens EXACTLY ONCE in the final render path, and output guards run on the model text BEFORE hydration. Never let the model see real values it doesn't need; never let pseudonyms reach the user. Pseudonymized text is not anonymous: style, context, and rare facts re-identify (Netflix-prize result, 2008).

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: Distinguish on-violation from on-failure behavior in guardrail orchestration.
flashcards.a: On VIOLATION (guard matched): pass, fix (deterministic transform like redaction), re-ask with feedback for FORMAT defects (cap retries), block for semantic/irreparable violations, escalate to human. On FAILURE (guard errored or timed out): the fail-open vs fail-closed decision, made PER RISK: PII scan for internal summarizer fails open with alarm; jailbreak classifier for a refund agent fails closed. Industry quietly defaults to fail-open; that default is how incidents happen.

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: Where can guardrails run, and why do layers beat one chokepoint?
flashcards.a: In-app (in-process/sidecar): only place with request context, untrusted tool results, and risk tiers. Gateway/proxy: org-wide policy and egress masking (Presidio + LiteLLM recipe, so PII never reaches the provider). Platform: Azure/Bedrock filters, always-on baseline; Bedrock's ApplyGuardrail API runs guards without invoking the model. A single gateway guard cannot see tool results or downstream actions, and its failure is a single total bypass. The guard that matters most is often on the ACTION (tool tiers), not the text.

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: What documented platform-filter failure semantics must you design around in Azure OpenAI?
flashcards.a: Bad input prompt returns HTTP 400. Filtered completion returns finish_reason=content_filter. If the CONTENT FILTER SYSTEM ITSELF errors, the request returns 200 with content UNFILTERED, with an error object in content_filter_results telling you so. That is a documented fail-open you must monitor; 'the platform handles it' silently becomes 'the platform skipped it'.

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: What do Bedrock Guardrails and OpenAI moderation each cover?
flashcards.a: Bedrock: 6 content categories including Prompt Attack (jailbreak + prompt injection + prompt leakage), denied topics (e.g. blocking investment advice), word filters, PII block/mask with custom regex (probabilistic), contextual grounding checks, automated reasoning checks, versioned guardrails, ApplyGuardrail standalone API; blocked content appears as PLAINTEXT in invocation logs. OpenAI moderation: FREE, omni-moderation-latest, 13 categories with 0-1 scores, text and image (up to 20 MB), inline Responses API scores covering tool-call arguments and outputs but not tool names/descriptions; the model upgrades continuously so custom thresholds need recalibration.

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: How do canary-based leak detection work, and what are their two failure modes?
flashcards.a: Generate a high-entropy random token per session, embed it in the system prompt or tool results, and substring-scan every egress surface (model output, tool-call args, logs, summaries) for it. A hit means content from inside the trust boundary leaked outward. Failure modes: an attacker who can strip or encode the canary bypasses the scan, and it detects THAT a leak occurred, not WHAT or WHERE TO. It's a tripwire, not a seal; pair with egress allowlists and tool-tier backstop. A canary in a model-constructed search query is exfiltration-in-progress: block, alert, revoke tool access.

flashcards.topic: Guardrails In/Out: Guardrails AI, NeMo, Validation Layers, PII, Toxicity
flashcards.q: How do you measure guardrail efficacy without hurting UX?
flashcards.a: Two corpora, two numbers, reported together: recall on a red-team suite in CI (per-guard catch rate), and FALSE-POSITIVE RATE on sampled benign production traffic (the product-killer; XSTest, arXiv 2308.01263, exists to measure exaggerated safety). Monitor score-distribution drift (moderation models upgrade silently), guard-error rate as an SLO, and the blocked-benign to blocked-malicious ratio for the product team. Roll out new guards in shadow mode (log-only) before enforcing. Efficacy is a rate of adaptation, not a completed state.
